name: Chip supply
summary: China's rare-earth export pause expires 10 Nov with no formal extension; AI chip shares sold off
state: China's suspension of its rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, and as of 5 Nov Beijing had published no formal notice extending it, though the wider US–China trade truce runs to 10 Jan 2027 (Motley Fool). The Nasdaq fell more than 5% as AI-linked stocks sold off around 5 Nov (Just Security). No TSMC or Samsung output stoppage had been reported as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Device makers and carmakers that rely on rare-earth magnets are most exposed if controls return. Consumers are unlikely to see shortages immediately.
rubric_hit: Watch: possible return of rare-earth export controls on 10 Nov; no major TSMC/Samsung disruption

sources.title: Motley Fool — China's rare-earth export pause expires Nov. 10

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
